exposure: Women intending to give birth in a birth center
Birth center vs. hospital labor ward
Women intending to give birth in a hospital labor ward
Birth setting (birth center vs. hospital labor ward)
cohort: Women in New South Wales, Australia who intended to give birth in a birth center, matched with women who intended to give birth in the co-located hospital labor ward
finding: Women who intended to give birth in a birth center had significantly lower rates of postpartum hemorrhage, retained placenta, postpartum infection, cesarean section, and episiotomy, and higher rates of breastfeeding at discharge compared to women who intended to give birth in a hospital labor ward.
mod_finding: Rates of postpartum hemorrhage, retained placenta, postpartum infection, cesarean section, and episiotomy were significantly lower in women intending birth center births compared to those intending hospital births, while breastfeeding rates were higher.
